messages:
Anya: Quick sync — after the V2 rollout, I want to propose a 3-day 'refinement slice' to shave down customer pain. Goals: ship the highest-impact fix, add basic cost telemetry, and defer bigger UX polish unless trivial. Items I see:
- streaming truncation bug (seen in ~12 enterprise customers)
- post-edit UX friction (accept/undo flow) — low risk but visible
- telemetry for token-cost spikes per-route

Devin: Repro'ed the truncation. Looks like a KV-cache tokenization edge-case when chunks boundary align. I have a patch but need a model-compat regression run. Rough estimate: 1 eng ~1.5 days + test matrix.

Sasha: For post-edit UX I can do a minimal change: collapse the suggestion menu, add an 'apply suggestion' primary button. Mocks: ~2 days; dev work ~1 day if we keep it shallow. We can also ship a CSS tweak today as a stopgap.

Liam: Support signal: 5 paid customers reported interruptions; 7 more smaller accounts see degraded responses. Severity = medium-high; customers asking for ETA. I'd push bug earlier if possible.

Mika: Telemetry ask: we need per-route token histograms and a simple alert when 2x baseline. Baseline calc can be rolling 7-day median. Backend effort ~2 days but we can scope to a single high-traffic route for the canary.

Anya: Suggestion for prioritization: (1) streaming truncation fix + canary, (2) minimal telemetry for the canary route, (3) UX polish if we have leftover capacity or can do a CSS hotpatch. This keeps customer impact low and gives us observability to catch regressions.

Devin: Agree — bug + telemetry. If we can run a 5% canary asap we can validate patch against production traffic. I can do the patch + e2e and request canary deploy.

ReleaseBot: ReleaseBot: Canary window available Thu 11:00-14:00 UTC. Reminder: attach runbook and add "canary-5pct" tag. Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/stream-truncation.md

Sasha: I can scope the CSS stopgap today (10-30m). I'll also prepare a one-screen mock in case we can squeeze the full UX in Day 3.

Liam: I'll assemble the customer list for early canary opt-in and draft comms offering rollback support. Also will surface the issue to account owners.

Anya: Decision: 3-day plan
Day 1: Patch + unit/regression tests (owner: Devin)
Day 2: Telemetry for canary route + deploy 5% canary (owner: Mika + Release)
Day 3: Monitor, roll, customer comms, and optional minimal UX ship (owner: Sasha + Liam)
Meeting: 30m grooming tomorrow 9:30am PT. @Devin @Mika @Sasha pls ack.

Devin: Ack — PR by EOD with test notes.

Mika: Ack — will start telemetry scaffold and point at route /api/generate-main.

Sasha: Ack — will post CSS hotpatch and a quick mock.

Liam: Ack — customer list + templates queued.

Anya: Thanks team :thumbsup: I'll create the epic with label refinement/mini-sprint and set priorities P1 (bug), P2 (telemetry), P3 (UX). Will link the canary runbook and assign owners. If anything blocks the canary, escalate in this thread.

Devin: Quick note — deployment snippet I'll use:
```
deploy --service inference --image v2-fix-2026-03-21 --canary 5% --route blue
```
Will also add a metric assertion to fail canary if truncation rate > 0.5%.

Mika: I'll add the alert: token_cost_spike_rate > 2x baseline and truncation_rate > 0.1% to the canary dashboard.

Anya: Perfect. If no objections, I'll post the Jira tickets and calendar invite. Closing for now, will follow up in grooming.

ReleaseBot: ReleaseBot: Canary slot reserved for v2-fix-2026-03-21 Thu 11:00 UTC — owner: Devin. Good luck :)
